blocks.text: The mode is the value or values that appear most frequently in a dataset. From a biological perspective, it can be used to understand the most common characteristics or traits in a biological sample, such as the most frequent number of flowers on a plant, the most common size of seeds in a population, or the most frequently occurring weight in a sample of animals.
There is no specific formula to calculate mode in ungrouped data. The mode is simply the value or values that appear more frequently in a data set.
For grouped data the mode can be calculated by using the given formula:

blocks.text_alt: Mode = l + (fm − f₁) / [(fm − f₁) + (fm − f₂)] × h

items: l = lower boundary of the modal class.
fm = frequency of the model class.
F₁ = frequency of the class before the modal class.
f₂ = frequency of the class after the modal class.
h = class width (the difference between upper and lower limits of any class interval).

blocks.text: 'model class' should read 'modal class', the class with the highest frequency. (F₁ is the f₁ of the formula.)
blocks.title: Book correction
Steps to calculate the Mode for ungrouped data with example
blocks.problem: A biologist studied the height (cm) of ten plants in a garden. The heights of plants are 50cm, 60 cm, 50 cm, 55 cm, 50 cm, 65 cm, 60 cm, 70 cm, 55 cm and 50 cm.
steps: Step 1: Arrange the data in ascending order.
50 cm, 50 cm, 50 cm, 50 cm, 55 cm, 55 cm, 60 cm, 60 cm, 65 cm, 70 cm.
Step 2: Count the frequency of each value.
blocks.answer: The number 50 appears the most frequently i.e. 4 times. Therefore, the mode for this dataset is 50 cm.

blocks.text: Steps to calculate the Mode for grouped data with example
Consider we are studying the weight (kg) distribution of animals in a zoo.
